summary.title: Hacker's Delight, 2nd Edition
summary.one_liner: A book of practical, proof-backed bit-manipulation and integer arithmetic tricks, from rightmost-bit hacks to division by constants, CRC, Hamming codes and Hilbert curves.
takeaways: Covers classic bit tricks such as manipulating rightmost bits, overflow detection, min/max and sign functions without branches.
Explains how to divide by constants using multiply-high and shifts, including signed and unsigned cases and methods without multiply-high.
Includes chapters on population count, leading/trailing zero counting, bit reversal, compress/expand and permutations.
Adds newer chapters on CRC, Hamming error-correcting codes, Hilbert curve and floating-point conversions, with exercises and answers.
summary.summary: This is the second edition of Henry S. Warren's book (Addison-Wesley, 2012/2013, 512 pages) collecting programming hacks and algorithms for integer and bit-level computation. The table of contents is organized by topic: basic logical and arithmetic idioms, power-of-2 boundaries, bit counting, searching words, rearranging bits, multiplication, integer division (including by constants), elementary functions, number bases, Gray code, CRC, error-correcting codes, Hilbert's curve, and floating-point. The second edition adds CRC and ECC chapters, more division-by-constant coverage, and exercises with answers. The listing notes that it derives the branch-free techniques with proofs rather than presenting them as a catalogue; the page itself offers only the table of contents and publisher details, so the depth of individual methods is not shown here.
